items.title: Ralph LaLama interviewed by Monk Rowe, Utica, New York, May 23, 2010
items.q: Stanley I knew, he’s a writer, I like Stanley actually... Stanley Crouch used to book him [Sadik Hakim]... he wrote an article in the Village Voice... talking about... Ralph LaLama

ctx.x: You are a middle-aged white guy. That’s my astute observation. Does that affect getting gigs?

You know, okay, that’s a great question. I’ll go back to when I grew up. I grew up near Pittsburgh in a place called Aliquippa, West Aliquippa, Pennsylvania. And my grandmother, my mother’s mother, lived in a part of Aliquippa which was called Plan Eleven. Now Plan Eleven was all black except one white family, hers. Okay? And when I was a kid we would go there on Sunday to see my grandparents and hang out in the yard and next to the yard was another ball field, where the cats would play, the neighborhood would…
on the jazz scene where there’s supposed to be racial stuff. And I’ll tell you another story. You ever heard of Stanley Crouch?
